units.title: A neoplasm is not automatically malignant
units.lesson: A neoplasm is an abnormal growth of tissue. The term includes benign and malignant examples. The word alone does not establish invasive behaviour or spread. When answering an exam definition, separate the category “neoplasm” from the additional evidence needed to characterize biological behaviour.
units.question: Which statement about a neoplasm is correct?
choices: It may be benign or malignant
units.explanation: Neoplasm includes benign and malignant growths.
rationales: Malignancy is not inherent in the term.
Neoplasm is not synonymous with infection.

units.title: Dysplasia is cellular abnormality
units.lesson: Dysplasia describes abnormal cells within a tissue. It is not synonymous with cancer, although some dysplastic changes can progress. The nature and extent of abnormalities matter. A definition is not an individual prognosis; avoid replacing uncertainty with a claim that every dysplasia will progress or that none can.
units.question: Which best describes dysplasia?
choices: Abnormal cells that are not automatically cancer
units.explanation: Dysplasia denotes cellular abnormality, not automatic malignancy.

units.title: Understand tissue examination
units.lesson: Biopsy means obtaining cells or tissue for examination. A pathologist can assess cellular and tissue features that are not available from a surface description alone. The report is interpreted with clinical information. This explains the role of tissue evidence without teaching how to perform a biopsy or selecting a technique for a patient.
units.question: Which type of evidence can a biopsy provide?
units.explanation: Biopsy material enables examination of cells or tissue.

units.title: Invasion and metastasis differ
units.lesson: Malignant cells can invade nearby tissue. Metastasis means spread to another body site and formation of secondary disease there. Local invasion and distant spread are related concepts but not synonyms. A metastatic tumour retains the identity of its primary cancer rather than being renamed solely for its new location.
units.question: What does metastasis describe?
choices: Only a change in tooth colour
Spread of cancer to another body site
units.explanation: Metastasis concerns spread beyond the primary site.

units.question: A fictional primary cancer at site A forms a secondary deposit at site B. Which description is best?
choices: Metastatic disease identified by its primary origin
A new unrelated primary at B solely because of location

units.explanation: A metastatic deposit retains its primary cancer identity.
rationales: Location alone does not create a new primary identity.
